lesson_title: Inside a Salon's Money: Where Every Rand Goes
hook_text: A salon made R20 000 this month. So why did the owner only keep R3 700?
clip_script: R20 000 came in: haircuts, braids, manicures and product sales. That is income. Now the money going out: products R4 200, assistant's wages R6 000, rent R4 000, electricity R1 300, data, adverts, bank charges. R16 300 in expenses. R20 000 minus R16 300: R3 700 profit. Then the twist: rent and wages are fixed, the same every month even when the salon is empty. Products are variable, they rise with customers. And the R800 groceries from the cash box? Not an expense. Drawings. Know your in, your out and your fixed costs, and you know your business.
visual_style: A whiteboard salon with money arrows flowing in from customers and out to rent, wages, products and electricity, with fixed and variable labels.
mood: Clear and eye-opening, a behind-the-counter look.
pacing: A big income number, a rapid list of costs, then a calm profit reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list the fixed and variable costs of a business near your home.
